timestamp.guidesIntro: A Unix timestamp counts the seconds elapsed since midnight on 1 January 1970 UTC. It describes one absolute instant for every machine on earth, regardless of timezone.

guides.title: Why a Unix timestamp?
guides.text: It is a single unambiguous integer: sorting, comparing and storing it in a database is lighter and safer than any formatted date string.

guides.title: Seconds or milliseconds?
guides.text: JavaScript and Java produce 13 digits (milliseconds), while Python, PHP and Go produce 10 (seconds). This tool detects the unit from the length of the number.

guides.title: Leap seconds
guides.text: 27 leap seconds have been added to UTC so far. Unix time ignores them, so its drift against atomic clocks stays negligible for everyday calculations.

faqs.question: How is the Iranian timezone handled?
faqs.answer: Iran dropped daylight saving time in 2022, so Asia/Tehran is a fixed UTC+03:30. This tool reads your browser's local clock first and then renders the same absolute instant in UTC and ISO 8601.

faqs.question: Is any of my data uploaded?
faqs.answer: No. There is not a single network request: the conversion is plain JavaScript on the instant your browser already knows.

faqs.question: Why can the Jalali result differ by a day?
faqs.answer: Conversion uses the Khayyam astronomical algorithm (jalaali-js), which starts the year at the vernal equinox. Hand-made calendars can disagree by one day in a handful of years.

faqs.question: What does a negative timestamp mean?
faqs.answer: Negative values point to dates before 1 January 1970. This tool supports them and shows the equivalent date.

dateDiff.privacyIntro: The fixed Iranian solar holidays (Nowruz, 22 Bahman, 29 Esfand, …) ship as a local dataset inside this app, and Thursday plus Friday are removed from working days as the Iranian weekend.

privacyPoints.title: Shifting lunar holidays
privacyPoints.text: Religious holidays move every year and are announced by the official calendar authority, so they are never guessed. Add them from the “Day events” card on the timestamp tool to make business-day math exact.

privacyPoints.title: Browser-only storage
privacyPoints.text: Your custom holidays live in this browser's localStorage. Nothing is uploaded, tracked or analysed.

privacyPoints.title: No network dependency
privacyPoints.text: Every calculation keeps working with the network disconnected, because the page never talks to a server.

faqs.question: How are Iranian working days counted?
faqs.answer: Any day in the range that is neither a Thursday nor a Friday and is not on the official holiday list counts as a working day. Add your own holidays and they join that list too.

faqs.question: How is the year/month difference derived?
faqs.answer: With calendar borrowing: years and months follow the real calendar lengths, and the remaining hours, minutes and seconds come from a clock subtraction.

faqs.question: How do you know a Jalali year is a leap year?
faqs.answer: The Khayyam algorithm evaluates the vernal equinox; a year is leap when Esfand has 30 days. Gregorian leap years follow the 4/100/400 rule.

faqs.question: Why can the distance differ slightly from manual counting?
faqs.answer: Ranges with different clock times (say 14:00 → 09:00) split a day. The metric cards therefore show both the raw distance (total seconds) and the whole calendar days.

password.faqTitle: Frequently asked questions about password security

faqs.question: How is this different from Math.random()?
faqs.answer: Math.random is not suitable for security; this tool uses the browser's Web Crypto API directly, so its output is not designed to be predictable.

faqs.question: How long should a standard password be?
faqs.answer: At least 16 random characters is recommended for general use; more length increases the key space and resistance to guessing.

faqs.question: Is a multi-word passphrase secure?
faqs.answer: Yes. Random 4- or 5-word passphrases are both secure and memorable thanks to their length and huge number of combinations.

faqs.question: Why is there an option to avoid similar characters?
faqs.answer: To prevent mistakes when reading or typing characters such as 1 and l, or 0 and O.
